summary: Reviewed all newly displayed narrative fields against captured definitions, retained prior corrections, and clarified vacancy denominators, household-stock scope, income coverage and unverified timing.

decision_edits.M184101:1: Excluded within household_income as a capacity choice. This is mean income per employed resident, including employer CPF and excluding bonus; it may proxy purchasing capacity but is not household income. Its captured history is shorter than several alternatives. The annual household median was preferred for household-level scope, with a loss of quarterly timeliness.
decision_edits.M016081:1: Excluded within household_income as a capacity choice. Aggregate nominal personal disposable income is not income per household and can combine population and price changes with income changes. The median among resident employed households was preferred for that specific population; it is not a measure of every household or of the typical property buyer.
decision_edits.M400391:2: Excluded within housing_supply as a capacity choice. This is the total non-landed private residential pipeline across development stages, not an unpurchased or unsold subset. The expectations channel may matter, but completion timing and cancellations prevent interpreting the pipeline as a completion forecast. The vacant-stock measure was preferred for current absorption context; incremental predictive value has not been established.
decision_edits.M183111:7: Excluded within labour_market as a capacity choice. Total year-end employment includes resident and non-resident employees, self-employed persons and migrant domestic workers. Some workers do not require an ordinary separate rental unit, but these data do not establish how most workers are housed or a strong correlation with GDP. Quarterly resident unemployment was preferred for resident labour-market stress; total employment remains potentially informative.
decision_edits.M810361:5: Selected for affordability context among resident employed households. The household employment-income median is less sensitive to very high incomes than the mean, but it does not represent non-employed households, all households or the typical property buyer. It includes employer CPF and annual bonus allocation, is nominal, and is not take-home income. Its annual frequency limits near-term monitoring.
decision_edits.M400751:1.1: Excluded within housing_supply as a capacity choice. Total HDB flats are public-housing stock, not new additions. This is distinct from private-sector vacancy and may inform the HDB resale outcome; private vacancy does not fully substitute for it. The model preferred other dashboard channels, but this does not establish that HDB stock lacks explanatory or predictive value.
decision_edits.M400841:2: Selected as the housing-supply slack signal. Vacant completed private homes may provide absorption context relevant to sale prices and rents, depending on demand. The matching completed-stock series is retained in the captured data and used to derive vacancy rates, although it is outside the selected dashboard. The count does not identify active listings or establish predictive value.

M182342:2.lag: Housing decisions may adjust after labour-market changes, but the supplied metadata and correlations do not establish unemployment as an early business-cycle indicator or a fixed response delay.
M182342:2.rents: Weaker resident labour conditions may strain rent budgets among affected resident households. The effect on aggregate rents remains uncertain because tenant composition, incomes and housing supply also matter; this series does not identify household splits or lease-renewal outcomes.

M810361:5.sales: Higher nominal median employment income among resident employed households could support affordability and debt servicing within that group. Employer CPF and bonus treatment, household composition, inflation and lending rules prevent interpreting this as universal take-home purchasing power.
M810361:5.rents: Higher nominal employment income among resident employed households may support rent affordability within that group. Its relationship with aggregate rents remains uncertain because tenant coverage, inflation, employer CPF contributions, bonus allocation and household composition differ from cash resources available for rent.
M810361:5.limitations: The series covers resident households with at least one employed member and excludes households with no employed member. It includes employer CPF contributions and annual bonus allocation, is nominal, and is not a wage index, income per household member or take-home income. It does not represent all households, all tenants or the typical property buyer. Supply conditions and borrowing rules also matter.
M810361:5.lag: Annual observation frequency limits short-term timing analysis. Changes in affordability could feed into purchase and rental decisions gradually, but the supplied metadata do not establish an exact within-year reference date, historical publication availability or a fixed behavioural lag.

M810371:1.limitations: This is a stock of resident households. Its changes are net changes and cannot separately identify gross formation or dissolution. Tenure choices, eligibility, sampling variability and source changes limit housing-demand interpretation; publication-time historical availability is not reconstructed.
M810371:1.lag: Annual household-stock changes provide structural demand context, not a measure of gross household formation. Housing responses may develop gradually, subject to tenure and affordability; the supplied series does not establish a fixed behavioural lag or a historical publication delay.
M810371:1.rents: Growth in resident household counts may support rental demand among households that rent rather than own, subject to tenure choices, affordability and eligibility. The aggregate count does not identify households' ages, independence status or actual rental arrangements.

M400841:2.limitations: This series counts vacant completed private homes rather than active sale or rental listings. The matching completed-stock series is retained in the captured data and used to calculate vacancy rates, although it is outside the selected dashboard. Count changes can reflect changes in total stock as well as vacancy shares. Coverage excludes HDB flats and Executive Condominiums.
M400841:2.lag: Vacancy is a quarter-end stock measure. Price or rent responses may occur as listings, tenancies and owners' expectations adjust, but the supplied data do not establish a fixed response delay or that later effects exceed immediate effects.

M700071:23.limitations: This is a month-end observation of a three-month compounded benchmark, expressed as an annual percentage rate; it is not a monthly average or an individual mortgage quote. Actual borrowing costs depend on lender spreads, contract types, repricing dates and policy measures. No additional smoothing or interpolation was performed.

notes: All original model decisions and narratives are preserved in original_selection.json. Selected IDs, raw observations, evidence IDs and statistical calculations are unchanged.
Pipeline correction: evaluation metadata for M400391:2 defines total non-landed pipeline across development statuses. It does not identify unpurchased units or substantiate double-counting.
Employment correction: metadata for M183111:7 identifies resident and non-resident employment coverage, including migrant domestic workers. No tenure-share or GDP-correlation evidence was supplied.
Income corrections preserve the distinction between a per-employed-person mean, aggregate disposable income and the median among resident employed households.
Unemployment lag wording is now conditional; early-cycle behavior was not established. Annual seasonal revisions are stated in the supplied mechanism notes and were retained.
These editorial corrections are review judgements grounded in the captured definitions, not additional model output or automatic semantic proof.
The prior six decision edits and three narrative edits are retained. Newly displayed narratives were separately reviewed; field-level labels identify every explicit edit.
Vacancy correction: M400841:1 is preserved in evaluations and research. The denominator is outside the selected dashboard, not absent from the captured data.
Household counts measure stocks, not gross formation or age-specific tenancy. The income measure is conditional on at least one employed member, not on all tenants or all sources of household income.
Annual frequency and contemporaneous quarterly measures do not establish within-period reference dates, fixed behavioural lags or relative magnitudes of immediate and delayed effects.
The three-month compounded SORA benchmark is sampled at month-end; not a monthly average does not mean that it is not a compounded average.
No new data, model selection, numerical calculation or network/model call is introduced by this presentation.
